transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-26
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE); Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE); Laura Chen (PortalHealth Procurement); Marcus Vega (PortalHealth Head of Security); Evelyn Ross (PortalHealth Legal); Tom Alvarez (PortalHealth FinOps); Priya Sinha (PortalHealth Eng)

Summary:
Quick procurement and legal alignment to clear MSA/DPA redlines, confirm security attachments (SOC2, KMS), pricing approval path and PO gating. Agreement to share redlines and run a short private deploy benchmark. Legal deep-dive to be scheduled.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA exceptions
- Data residency, KMS/HSM and encryption at rest
- SOC 2 / audit artifacts and pen test dates
- Pricing approval path and PO timeline / FinOps questions
- Private deployment options (VPC, on-prem) vs Redwood hosted SLA implications

00:00:00 Jared: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um I'll kick off quick agenda — procurement, legal redlines, security checklist and then pricing/PO path. If we run over we can follow up, is that fine?
00:00:18 Laura: Yep that works for us, thanks Jared. We're mainly here to understand our gating steps and see if we can hit September procurement window.
00:00:27 Marcus: And I'll focus on security items — KMS, audit logs, access controls. We looked at the public docs but have a few clarifications.
00:00:36 Jared: Perfect, I'll hand to Sofia for the technical callouts first.
00:00:41 Sofia: Hi all, quick note on private deployment modes — Redwood Private can be deployed into customer VPC or on-prem via our private control plane. For PortalHealth specifically, per our earlier note, the KMS integration supports customer-managed keys via standard HSM/KMS vendors, and we also produce audit logs with request-level tracing. That said, I want to call out two tradeoffs: 1) Dedicated/private adds about 10–15% delta on base price due to reserved capacity and longer retention for logs, and 2) if you want on-prem truly air-gapped there are packaging constraints — we need some initial connectivity for control-plane bootstrap unless you go fully appliance mode which adds time.
00:01:35 Priya: Sorry can I jump — what does the "bootstrap" look like? We have strict environment controls.
00:01:40 Sofia: Sure, the bootstrap is a one-time handshake for license and telemetry (no customer data required) so we can validate artifacts. We can also do an offline SHA-based license exchange if you need zero egress. I've put that in the notes.
00:01:57 Marcus: Okay that helps. Can you also confirm whether KV cache or any tokenized data is stored outside the VPC?
00:02:06 Sofia: Good question. KV cache (sometimes shows up as K V cash in some transcripts, haha) is kept within the customer's VPC when you choose Private. In Hosted mode we use encrypted managed caches but we have contracts to ensure no customer tensors or full prompts are persisted beyond ttl unless customer opts into longer retention.
00:02:30 Evelyn: From Legal side, our counsel wants to know the jurisdiction for data storage and whether Redwood will accept certain DPA clauses — subprocessor list, notification windows, and liability caps.
00:02:44 Jared: We'll send the current subprocessor list and the latest SOC2 and pen test report. On liability caps, we usually have a standard commercial cap; we can discuss specifics in the legal deep-dive.
00:02:55 Evelyn: Also would like to request the schedule for SOC2 audit reports — date range and any open exceptions.
00:03:03 Sofia: Marcus, I can share the SOC2 snapshot and the last pen test summary; there are no open exceptions for the last cycle. I'll attach the artifacts.
00:03:12 Marcus: Great, please do. Also about KMS — do you support customer HSM through AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure KeyVault? And do you have attestations for admin separations?
00:03:25 Sofia: Yes, we support those three clouds' KMS integrations and can configure customer-managed keys with rotation policies. Admin separation is enforced in our role model; we can provide architecture docs that show RBAC and SSO paths (Saml / S A M L integration).
00:03:40 Tom: On pricing — is the 10–15% uplift per month or is that a commitment spread? Our FinOps needs to forecast commit vs overage.
00:03:50 Jared: The delta I mentioned was a rough ballpark for private reserved capacity; actual pricing depends on commit term and model footprint. For committed Dedicated pools we do monthly committed slots, with overage rates that are lower than hosted. We'll provide a pricing workbook.
00:04:06 Tom: Who signs the PO? We need exact billing entity and any required billing CLAs, and our procurement wants a sample PO template.
00:04:14 Jared: We'll include a sample PO template in the package and clarify the billing entity — Redwood Inc. with tax id and billing address.
00:04:21 Laura: Our procurement committee needs two approvals: security (Marcus) and commercial (me) then legal clearance. We're targeting first pass approval on Sept 6 so we can issue PO mid-September.
00:04:33 Jared: Good, we'll aim to get docs to you before Aug 29 so you have time.
00:04:38 Evelyn: On the DPA — there are one or two clauses we'd like to propose: a 30-day deletion SLA for customer data upon termination, and a stronger notification window for breaches (48 hours). Are those negotiable?
00:04:50 Jared: We can accept the deletion timeline; breach notification we typically do 72 hours but we can escalate legal to discuss 48 hours if it's a hard requirement. We'll call that out in the redline.
00:05:02 Sofia: For the deletion path, on Private we can implement a certified purge run. On Hosted we have documented retention windows and can do verified deletions with attestation if required.
00:05:12 Marcus: Excellent. Another technical ask — we need request-level audit logs with immutable storage for 12 months. Is that supported and are those logs exportable to our SIEM?
00:05:24 Sofia: Yes, we can stream audit logs to your logging endpoint (S3, BigQuery, or used SIEM connectors) and set retention to 12 months; there is some extra cost for long-term retention.
00:05:36 Priya: For the private deploy test, can we run a subset of live traffic that resembles production? We have sample privacy-classified data, is that okay?
00:05:45 Sofia: For benchmarking we prefer synthetic or anonymized samples. If you need to use real-like PII then we recommend a sanitized dataset or work under a secure enclave with a DPA addendum.
00:05:58 Tom: What's the typical timeline for a pilot to go from contract to test environment?
00:06:04 Jared: Usually 2–4 weeks for Private depending on legal redlines, and about a week for hosted trials. If you prioritize the procurement lane we can compress it.
00:06:12 Laura: Sounds reasonable. Marcus, anything else on security?
00:06:16 Marcus: One more — does Redwood support MFA + SSO enforced for all admin accounts and can you show us the provisioning flow?
00:06:23 Sofia: Yes MFA + SSO (SAML/V S A M L) are standard; provisioning can be SCIM-based for automated user sync. We'll include a provisioning runbook.
00:06:34 Evelyn: On legal redlines, we'll mark up the MSA and DPA. Who should we send redlines to?
00:06:39 Jared: Send to me and I'll circulate to legal; I'll coordinate with our legal ops and loop Sofia when technical clarifications are needed.
00:06:46 Evelyn: Alright.
00:06:48 [02:10] Jared: Quick note on competitors, PortalHealth mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI as comparative options — one difference we emphasize is predictable unit economics and the Private model for data residency.
00:06:58 Laura: Pricing question: can you provide a committed pricing table vs on-demand so Finance can model both?
00:07:04 Jared: Absolutely yes, we'll include committed vs on-demand lines and show example scenarios for average token counts per session.
00:07:12 Tom: Please also include a sample invoice and clarifying line items — per-token, per-embedding, and reserved pool charges.
00:07:20 Jared: Will do.
00:07:22 [12:05] Sofia: Technical nuance — when you pick a model, you can pin versions. We also support automatic fallback policies that route requests to smaller quantized variants if capacity is constrained. This affects latency but can save cost.
00:07:39 Priya: Can we lock model versions for compliance audits?
00:07:42 Sofia: Yes, you can pin and we keep immutable model manifests for audit.
00:07:47 Marcus: For incident response, we need an SLA and runbook for high-severity events. What are your standard SLA windows?
00:07:55 Jared: Our enterprise SLA for Dedicated/private is 99.9% uptime with priority escalation and a 2-hour initial response for Sev1. We'll attach the SLA pdf and on-call contacts.
00:08:06 Marcus: Good.
00:08:08 [18:30] Evelyn: A legal meta question — are you open to a mutual indemnification carveout for privacy-related claims?
00:08:16 Jared: We generally stick to customer-data indemnity with limited mutuality for IP claims. We'll have legal discuss specifics in the deep-dive.
00:08:24 Laura: One operational ask — can you provide a one-page map of required signoffs and estimated days so procurement can plan?
00:08:31 Jared: Yes I'll draft a one-pager with signoff owners: Security, Legal, Procurement, FinOps and target dates.
00:08:37 Tom: If we need expedited procurement, is there a short-term commercial arrangement?
00:08:42 Jared: We can provide a short pilot contract with limited term and pre-agreed rates to unblock technical validation while legal finishes the full MSA.
00:08:50 Laura: That could be helpful.
00:08:52 [25:10] Sofia: On observability — Redwood Console exposes per-route latency, token cost, and tracing hooks. We can set token-level cost alerts that feed to your FinOps.
00:09:02 Tom: Can those exports go to our billing system?
00:09:06 Sofia: Yes, we have billing exports and can supply CSVs or direct S3 exports for ingestion.
00:09:11 Marcus: For compliance, can we get a list of subprocessors?
00:09:15 Jared: We'll include the current subprocessor list with the redline packet.
00:09:18 [32:00] Evelyn: Any outstanding dependencies on our side to start the pilot?
00:09:23 Priya: We'll need an endpoint ACL, service account, and the sanitized dataset. Also procurement needs the sample PO.
00:09:29 Jared: Actionable then — I'll bundle: redlined MSA/DPA, subprocessor list, SOC2 + pen test, pricing workbook, PO sample, and the provisioning runbook. Sofia will provide the benchmark results separately.
00:09:41 Laura: Can you mark which items are critical path for our Sept 6 approval?
00:09:46 Jared: Yes I'll highlight critical docs in the package.
00:09:49 [40:05] Marcus: Slightly off-topic but do you provide attestations for data residency on a per-customer basis?
00:09:55 Sofia: We can provide an attestation letter for residency and encryption practices, yes. There may be a small processing lead-time.
00:10:02 Evelyn: For the DPA breach notification 48 hours ask, we'll escalate to legal; appreciate you being open to discuss.
00:10:08 Jared: Noted; we'll flag that as potential legal negotiation point.
00:10:12 [45:30] Jared: Quick recap of next steps: Jared — send redlines and docs by Aug 28; Sofia — private deploy benchmark by Sept 1; PortalHealth to confirm procurement owner and target PO date by Sept 2; schedule legal deep-dive week of Sept 7. Any last items?
00:10:27 Laura: Nope that's it, thanks everyone.
00:10:30 Jared: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the packet and calendar invite for legal deep-dive.

Attachments / references mentioned:
- MSA (current draft)
- DPA (current draft)
- Subprocessor list (will attach)
- SOC2 report & pen test summary
- Pricing workbook & sample PO
- Private deploy runbook and provisioning notes

End of transcript.
